newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil stocks close higher in heavy trading.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stocks close higher in heavy trading.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed with strong gains in heavy trading on Tuesday after positive news on U.S. interest rates and speculation that the government will succeed in enacting civil service reform, brokers said.
"There was strong buying at the end of the session and the market closed at its daily high," one broker said.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa .BVSP index of 48 most-traded shares ended up 1.26 percent at 10,506 points in hefty trade of 874 million reais ($825 million).
Brokers said the market absorbed an early wave of selling and later climed after news that the policy-making arm of the U.S. Federal Reserve decided to leave short-term interest rates unchanged.

The market surged late in the day as rumors circulated that the government may succeed in passing civil service reform as well as block opposition attempts to form a panel to investigate an alleged congressional cash-for-votes scheme.
"There was lots of buying in the last half hour," a trader said.
The rise among Brazilian blue chips was led by state oil monopoly Petrobras, which rose 4.33 percent to end at 253.00 reais.
Cia Vale do Rio Doce, the recently privatized mining concern, closed up 1.66 percent at 24.50 reais.
The pace, as usual, was set by bellwether Telebras, whose preferred shot up 1.35 percent to end at 134.70 reais, while its common shares rose 1.28 percent to end at 127.00 reais.
Brazilian power shares followed the trend, with the bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE rising 1.22 percent to end at 2,779 points.
